title: Triage of fire victims
stem: ED entrance. A fire in a restaurant has produced five casualties arriving together; resus has two free bays. You are the senior triage officer. Triage them and give the key first orders.
notes:
Checked against ATLS 10th (burns), the American Burn Association mass-casualty burn triage guidance (Saffle 2005; ABA 2021 update of the triage table by age and TBSA), British Burn Association referral criteria (2018), and UK/HK smoke-inhalation practice.

Priorities in fire victims: airway threat from inhalation injury (stridor, hoarseness, soot, facial burns) — intubate early; carbon monoxide (SpO2 is falsely normal; co-oximetry; 100% oxygen; consider hyperbaric oxygen for severe cases); cyanide from burning plastics (high lactate, shock, arrest — hydroxocobalamin 5 g IV); burn size and depth for fluids (>20% adults, >10% children, per ATLS). In a true mass-casualty burn event, patients with very large burns and advanced age may be triaged as expectant (ABA triage table); outside a mass casualty everyone gets full care. Cool burns with running water for 20 minutes within 3 hours; cover with cling film; keep warm. Refer to the burns centre by criteria (hands, face, perineum, circumferential, inhalation, >10% adults etc.).

Your notes list 'Triage of fire victim' as a topic only. Expectant triage of the 80-year-old applies only when resources are overwhelmed — say so aloud.

steps.label: Casualty A
steps.hint: Man, 25: hoarse voice, soft stridor, soot in the mouth, 20% partial-thickness burns.

opts.t: RED — resus bay now; anaesthetist for early intubation
opts.mark: A: RED for inhalation injury with early airway

opts.t: YELLOW — talking, so the airway is fine
opts.r: Stridor and hoarseness with soot = impending airway obstruction.

steps.label: Casualty B
steps.hint: Woman, 45: no burns, headache, confused (GCS 13), SpO2 99% on air.

opts.t: RED — suspected CO poisoning; 100% oxygen, co-oximetry, ECG
opts.mark: B: recognises CO poisoning despite normal SpO2

opts.r: Pulse oximetry reads carboxyhaemoglobin as oxygenated; confusion is a red flag.

steps.label: Casualty C
steps.hint: Man, 30: walking, 3% partial-thickness burns on the palm of his hand.

opts.t: GREEN — cool for 20 minutes, cling film, analgesia; refer to burns (hand)
opts.mark: C: GREEN with burn first aid and referral for hand burn

opts.r: Stable and walking; but hand burns do need burns referral.

steps.label: Casualty D
steps.hint: Woman, 80: about 90% full-thickness burns, GCS 3, agonal breathing. Mass casualty declared; resources overwhelmed.

opts.t: EXPECTANT — comfort care and analgesia; reassess if resources allow
opts.mark: D: EXPECTANT with comfort care (mass casualty only)

opts.t: RED — take the second resus bay
opts.r: In a declared mass casualty, survival is very unlikely and the bay is needed; outside a mass casualty she would get full care.

steps.label: Casualty E
steps.hint: Boy, 8: crying, 12% partial-thickness burns on the legs, capillary refill 3 s.

opts.t: RED — second resus bay; IV fluids (over 10% in a child), analgesia
opts.mark: E: RED child with >10% burns needing fluids

opts.t: GREEN — crying so airway is fine
opts.r: Over 10% TBSA in a child needs fluid resuscitation; poor perfusion.

steps.label: Orders
steps.hint: Oxygen for all smoke-exposed, co-oximetry, lactate, cyanide antidote ready, warm, burns centre.

opts.t: 100% oxygen for everyone exposed to smoke
Blood gas with COHb and lactate for A, B, E
Hydroxocobalamin available: give if lactate high and shocked

opts.r: Ice causes further injury and hypothermia; cool running water for 20 min.

qs.q: Why is SpO2 falsely reassuring in CO poisoning?
wrong: CO blocks the probe's light sensor
Hypothermia slows the probe response time a lot

qs.q: Antidote for cyanide from burning plastics?

qs.a: Cool running water for 20 minutes, within 3 hours
wrong: Ice packs for 1 hour to stop the burning
Butter or oil to seal the skin
Nothing until the burns team arrives
For everyone over 70 with over 20% burns
For any burn over 50% TBSA, always

badge.name: Smoke Reader
badge.flavor: Airway, CO, cyanide, size. SpO2 lies.

cards.q: Fire victim with normal SpO2 and confusion?
High lactate and shock after smoke inhalation?
Adults need formal burn fluids above…
